Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. | $f$ | $Y=-2$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ | ${f}_{X}$ | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | $X=-1$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ | | $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ | $0.05$ | $0.35$ | | $X=3$ | $0.05$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.35$ | | ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.2$ | $0.2$ | $0.35$ | $0.25$ | $1$ | Therefore, the probability mass functions for $X$ and $Y$ are given by the following tables:
$x$ $-1$ $1$ $3$
${f}_{X}(x)$ $0.3$ $0.35$ $0.35$

$y$ $-2$ $0$ $2$ $4$
${f}_{Y}(y)$ $0.2$ $0.2$ $0.35$ $0.25$

Now, we can compute the expected values for $X$ and $Y:$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\,{f}_{X}({x}_{i}) \\ & =(-1)\cdot 0.3+1\cdot 0.35+3\cdot 0.35 \\ & =-0.3+0.35+1.05 \\ & =1.1\end{aligned} $$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}\,{f}_{Y}({y}_{i}) \\ & =(-2)\cdot 0.2+0\cdot 0.2+2\cdot 0.35+4\cdot 0.25 \\ & =-0.4+0+0.7+1 \\ & =1.3.\end{aligned} $$ Finally, using the properties of expectation, we obtain $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[2X+4Y] & =2\text{E}[X]+4\,\text{E}[Y] \\ & =2(1.1)+4(1.3) \\ & =2.2+5.2 \\ & =7.4.\end{aligned} $$
